question: Critical analysis of on-policy self-distillation with a privileged-information teacher: signal versus bias, progressive loss of reasoning-path diversity, three levers (token weighting, nature of the PI, teacher dynamics with guidance decay), and what is established versus disputed in mathematical reasoning

S1.title: Self-Distilled Reasoner: On-Policy Self-Distillation for LLMs

S2.title: Why Does Self-Distillation (Sometimes) Degrade the Reasoning Capability of LLMs?

S3.title: On-Policy Self-Distillation with Sampled Demonstrations Reduces Output Diversity

S5.title: AMR-SD: Asymmetric Meta-Reflective Self-Distillation for Token-Level Credit Assignment

S6.title: When Are Teacher Tokens Reliable? Position-Weighted On-Policy Self-Distillation for Reasoning

S7.title: Entropy-Aware On-Policy Distillation of Language Models

S8.title: beta-OPSD: Deriving with Policy Optimization, Training with Self-Distillation

S10.title: HDPO: Hybrid Distillation Policy Optimization via Privileged Self-Distillation

S12.title: Rethinking Privileged Information in On-Policy Self-Distillation

S13.title: Privileged Solutions or Context-Induced Teacher Behavior? Dissecting On-Policy Self-Distillation

S14.title: Is More Privileged Information Better? Solution Traces to Problem-Solving Structure in Self-Distilled Reasoning

S15.title: Adaptive Teacher Exposure for Self-Distillation in LLM Reasoning

S16.title: Understanding Diversity Collapse in RLVR via the Lens of Overtraining

S17.title: Guidance Contrastive Token Credit Assignment for Discrete Policy Optimization

S18.title: Privileged Likelihood Is Not Automatically Value: Three Checks for Token Credit in OPSD

claims.text: OPSD trains a model on its own rollouts with a teacher that is the same model given privileged information such as a verified solution, while the student sees only the question
OPSD is reported as 4-8x more token-efficient than GRPO on mathematical reasoning benchmarks
A rich-context teacher suppresses expression of uncertainty and shortens responses, degrading math performance by up to 40 % in Qwen3-8B, DeepSeek-Distill-Qwen-7B and Olmo3-7B-Instruct
PI inflates teacher confidence on solution-implied tokens and deflates it on deliberation tokens such as Wait, Let, Maybe
Raw oracle solutions are linked to over-conditioned teacher distributions, implicit answer leakage and late-stage training collapse
On-policy self-distillation with sampled demonstrations shows decreasing rollout diversity and flattening pass@k, on graph path-finding and science QA, not mathematics
Position-weighted OPSD gains +1.0 and +1.1 Avg@12 on AIME 2024 and 2025
An entropy gate switches off the PMI term once teacher entropy collapses, across five models from 4B to 30B, with up to 11.5 points over GRPO and 2 to 10x fewer training steps
Entropy-aware forward/reverse KL mixing in an external-teacher setting is proposed because reverse KL reduces generation diversity
The correct reference gave no consistent benefit in OPSD and a solution from another problem can outperform the correct solution on several math benchmarks (Qwen3 1.7B-8B)
OP2SD, using a problem and solution from a different example, improves over the base model across three models and three math benchmarks and stays competitive with OPSD
OPSD gains do not necessarily come from access to the reference solution; the teacher's context-induced behaviour is an important factor
Trajectory-grounded guidance gives the highest aggregate question-only accuracy among compared methods, beating the full solution
Full teacher exposure is not reliably the best choice and teacher-student mismatch grows monotonically with exposure
A learnable reveal ratio adds +0.95, +2.05 and +2.33 Avg@12 over OPSD on AIME 24, AIME 25 and HMMT 25 for Qwen3-1.7B, 4B and 8B
Temporal annealing is part of AMR-SD, which names late-stage training collapse as the failure it addresses
Vanilla OPSD is the beta=1 member of a family interpolating between reference policy and privileged teacher, with return-to-go credit, outperforming vanilla OPSD on mathematical benchmarks
Privileged self-distillation applied only to all-fail prompts yields pass@4 +0.8 to +1.1 % and pass@8 +0.4 to +1.7 % while keeping greedy accuracy (Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B-Instruct)
In RLVR, Pass@1 improves while high-k Pass@k degrades under overtraining; restricting updates to zero-success problems lifts Pass@256 above the base model
A policy-gradient hybrid combining verifier advantages, reverse KL to the teacher and reference KL reports better stability and performance than RLVR and self-distillation baselines
On successful rollouts the teacher mechanism overwrites the student's own choices; reversing the signal on correct rollouts is proposed
Finding 1 verdict: the OPSD recipe trains and is token-efficient in the authors' settings (4-8x over GRPO, one team); independent replication is open
Finding 2: the only direct diversity-collapse measurement (falling rollout diversity, flattening pass@k) is on graph path-finding and science QA, not math
Finding 3: a position score predicts teacher-token reliability with AUROC 0.83 versus at most 0.57 for local uncertainty scores (Qwen3-4B setting)
Finding 3: entropy-aware distillation reports Pass@8 gains of +1.37, +2.39 and +5.05 on Qwen3-0.6B, 1.7B and 4B-Base across six math benchmarks
Finding 3: the title states privileged likelihood is not automatically value and proposes three checks for token credit in OPSD; content not specified (title only)
Finding 3: a contrastive method assigns per-token credit by contrasting positive and negative prompts and also covers text-to-image
Finding 4 verdict: the correct full solution is not necessary and not reliably best; a solution from another problem can outperform it
Finding 4: rich-context teachers suppress uncertainty, so the richest context can be harmful

conclusion: Self-distillation with privileged information gives a dense token-level signal but also a confidence-inflating bias whose effect on reasoning diversity in math is plausible and only indirectly supported; token weighting, the content of the privileged information and teacher exposure schedules are three levers that remain mostly open.
